thread.title: Silicon Valley's biggest stocks all climb — except Facebook

author: Marlize van Romburgh
title: Silicon Valley's biggest stocks all climb — except Facebook

organizations.name: bloomberg silicon valley high tech index

text: – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley Business Journal Feb 13, 2018, 2:00pm PST Updated Feb 13, 2018, 2:07pm PST Silicon Valley stocks largely settled down on Tuesday after a tumultuous week, with the exception of Facebook , which is facing criticism from lawmakers, publishers and advertisers even as new reports say smaller rival Snapchat (NYSE: SNAP) is gaining ground among younger users . The Bloomberg Silicon Valley High Tech Index closed up 1.84 percent, led by Symantec Corp (NASDAQ: SYMC). Ten of the 13 companies on the index closed up, including Juniper Networks (NYSE: JNPR), Cisco Systems (NASDAQ: CSCO), Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), HP Inc (NASDAQ: HPQ) and Oracle Corp. (NASDAQ: ORCL). Three stocks on the index fell: Facebook (NASDAQ: FB) dropped 1.58 percent, followed by Intel Corp. (NASDAQ: INTC), down 0.86 percent, and eBay (NASDAQ: EBAY), down 0.31 percent. Facebook's two years of strife were chronicled in a Wired magazine cover story published Monday that features a photo illustration of a battered and bruised Mark Zuckerberg on the cover. The 11,000-word article examines how the Menlo Park company and its embattled CEO have lurched from crisis to crisis, dealing with fake news, Russian propaganda, unhappy advertisers and obscene content. Facebook media executives prompted more eyebrows to rise Tuesday, when they told publishers who don't like its News Feed changes that they're welcome to leave. "If anyone feels that this isn't the right platform for them, then they should not be on Facebook," Campbell Brown , head of the company's news partnerships team, reportedly said . Otherwise, the region's stocks closed up amid relative calm in the U.S. financial markets, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average gaining 39.18 points on Tuesday and the S&P 500 up 0.26 percent. Among all Silicon Valley stocks, the top performers Tuesday were: • SunPower Corp. (NASDAQ: SPWR) surged 7.11 percent ahead of reporting its fourth-quarter financial results. • Infinera Corp. (NASDAQ: INFN) gained 3.85 percent. • Fortinet (NASDAQ: FTNT) closed up 3.53 percent. • VMware (NASDAQ: VMW) bounced 3 percent. • Arista Networks (NASDAQ: ANET) rose 2.83 percent. Along with Facebook, the worst performers among all Silicon Valley stocks Tuesday were: • Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ: SMCI) slumped 2.13 percent. • Trimble Inc (NASDAQ: TRMB) dropped 1.82 percent. • Cadence Design Systems (NASDAQ: CDNS) fell 1.81 percent. • Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. (NYSE: HPE) dipped 1.78 percent. – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley Business Journal Feb 13, 2018, 2:00pm PST Updated Feb 13, 2018, 2:07pm PST Related Content
